summary: <cite index="1-1,1-3">Oil jumped in early Asia trading as Middle East tensions accelerated, while the dollar held gains after hawkish comments from Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh fueled bets on a rate hike next month.</cite> <cite index="1-4">Global benchmark crude gained 2% at the open after the U.S. military on Sunday struck Iranian rocket launchers that were preparing to send mines into the Strait of Hormuz</cite>, intensifying energy-market volatility on the final trading day of August. <cite index="2-1">The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.9% or 464 points to close at 53,885.10</cite> on Friday, while <cite index="2-13">the S&P 500 was down 0.3% to finish at 7,711.76</cite> after Warsh's Jackson Hole speech raised inflation concerns. Crypto markets remained under pressure, with <cite index="18-1,18-3">Bitcoin opening at $77,695.48 on Monday, 0.7% lower than Sunday, before moving up to $77,999.80</cite>, while <cite index="18-15">U.S. airstrikes on Iranian rocket launchers over the weekend renewed hostilities in the Middle East, pushing oil prices higher and further raising expectations that rate hikes are imminent this year</cite>. Despite the pullback, <cite index="23-12">spot Bitcoin ETFs maintained relatively strong capital inflows, with cumulative net inflows of approximately $924 million from August 24 to 28</cite>, though institutional demand cooled somewhat as geopolitical risk dominated sentiment into Monday's session.

signals.title: Fed Chair Warsh hawkish Jackson Hole remarks fuel September rate hike bets
signals.desc: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech on inflation sparked market selloff Friday and lifted dollar, bond yields, pressuring equities and risk assets into Monday.

signals.title: U.S. strikes Iranian rocket launchers near Strait of Hormuz, oil surges 2%
signals.desc: Weekend military action by the U.S. against Iran reignited Middle East tensions, sending oil up 2% at Asia open and raising stagflation fears for equity markets.

signals.title: Chicago PMI manufacturing index plunges to 47.1, missing estimates
signals.desc: Chicago purchasing managers' index for manufacturing came in at 47.1 in August, significantly below the consensus estimate of 58, signaling contraction and weighing on sentiment.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs log $924M and $824M weekly inflows respectively
signals.desc: Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded cumulative net inflows of approximately $924 million from August 24 to 28, while Ethereum ETFs saw $824 million in five consecutive days of inflows, signaling resilient institutional demand.

signals.title: Markets position for heavy September economic data and earnings slate
signals.desc: Investors locking in profits on final August session ahead of first-week September events including jobs data, Fed policy signals, and corporate earnings, creating choppy conditions.

verdict: Risk-off tone dominates as hawkish Fed, Middle East strikes, and weak manufacturing data overshadow resilient crypto ETF inflows; defensive positioning likely into September data gauntlet.
